title: Wool Shed
shortDescription: A shed of wet wool and one honest lamp.
longDescription:
The shed smells of lanolin and peat-smoke. Fleeces hang on pegs, most of them still heavy with mist. A lamp burns because Foldhand Hobb does not trust the lane after dusk.
North is the mist-lane. South is the fold. West is Wren's door.

fixtures.name: Foldhand Hobb
fixtures.lookDescription: A mole in a wool vest, lamp-soot on his claws. Try talk hobb.
fixtures.examineDescription: A grey mole with his shoulders up, in a vest mended with the same fleece he hangs on the pegs. Lamp-soot is worked into the claws of both paws. He has walked this moor in weather that took sheep and gave none of them back, and he counts a fold twice before he says the number out loud. Ask him what is on the lane and he will tell you to ask Wren first.
fixtures.dialogue: Hobb is hanging wet fleece on the pegs and counting them under his breath as he goes. "Eleven pegs, ten full. That is not the number troubling me." He nods at the empty bell-loop by the door. "The flock went out counted and the bell did not come back with them. A bell does not wander off on its own, and a fold does not go quiet for nothing. If Wren has had you read the waystone already, talk hobb and I will show you a byre that should not be empty."

fixtures.name: Wool Pegs
fixtures.lookDescription: Pegs of wet fleece. Examine them.
fixtures.examineDescription: Most pegs are full. One near the door has a bell-loop and no bell. Hobb says the flock went out counted and the bell did not come home with them.
